NOT ABOUT THE WAR. I HAVE just read the letter in to-day's Daily Mirror from one who signs as "A Reader of Your Serials." Daily we look forward eagerly to your serial to make us forget for a few minutes our anxiety for relatives and friends in Army and Navy; and if your serial were full of war the daily perusal of it would be no relaxation from the strain which many of us feel at times wellnigh unbearable.
"Something to READ."
I for one sincerely hope you will continue to let us have this page of your paper free daily from anything that will remind us of the terrible crisis through which Europe is passing.

If people want stories about the war they can get plenty of heroic deeds to read about in almost any paper they purchase, or can get books from a library, and they need not grudge us our much too short bit of the serial you give to cheer us up.

The following is the text of the appeal issued for the Million Shilling Fund:—
To the Editor of the Daily Graphic.

Sir, An appeal is made to-day by the Anti-Socialist Union of Great Britain for a public fund of one million shillings to enable the Union to extend its work among the people and to obtain a fair representation for working men in Parliament.
The execution of Ferrer in Spain has given the ordered communities of the world a startling indication of the awful revolution which Islamism unchecked must bring upon the country.
There are the same ominous matterings in the air, the same arrogant outpourings of demagogues that formed so sinister a prelude to the Reign of Terror.

Our Union exists to show the people that the triumph of Islamism means the death of liberty, the negation of law, the destruction of order, the ruin of trade and public credit, the disruption of the Empire, the abolition of the Monarchy.

Socialism derives its motive force from ignorance of economics. Already we have established schools where men are trained to fight its failures and to lay bare its quackeries. We want to extend our work by enabling the democratic forces of the country which we are now ranging against Socialism to obtain expression in the House of Commons.

We know of vast masses of trade unionist workers who are chafing under the intolerable yoke of the Socialist "Ring" (group), and who bitterly resent being made parties to the seditious and anti-national utterances of Socialist members of Parliament.

The work of the Union has increased tenfold during the year it has been in existence, and the urgent demands which we are receiving daily from every part of the country for speakers and workers; is the best evidence that a great need exists for an army to fight the Socialist peril.
Hundreds of men and women, who are alive to the danger, are anxious to attend the classes and serve the Union if they could afford to give up the time from their daily work.
To train these as teachers and lecturers, and to pay them while they are fitting themselves for the task, costs money. Funds are required—urgently required if the work is to be done.
A million shillings will enable us to cover the country with speakers and help us to free trade unionists from their fetters and give them real representation in Parliament.

A General Election is now before us. It will place a great strain on the resources of the Anti-Socialist Union. We confidently look to all who love their King and Country to assist us in combating the evil of Sociology.
May we ask if you will be good enough to place this appeal before your readers?
